meta_description: The 9 Arrow electrical right-of-way safety manual covers OSHA-aligned policies, crew training, daily tailgate meetings and ongoing safety evaluation.
h1: Our electrical right-of-way safety manual for Texas ROW work
lede: The 9 Arrow electrical right-of-way safety manual sets out how we approach safety on electrical ROW clearing work in Texas. Below is a summary of what the manual covers and how to get a copy.

answer.q: What does the 9 Arrow electrical right-of-way safety manual cover?
answer.a: The 9 Arrow electrical right-of-way safety manual covers the company's commitment to safety in electrical ROW operations, including policies aligned with OSHA standards, employee training in hazard recognition, electrical awareness, first aid, equipment operation and emergency procedures, daily tailgate meetings, and ongoing evaluation of safety protocols for continuous improvement.

highlights: Training in hazard recognition and first aid
Daily tailgate meetings for crew members

sections.h2: Commitment to safety in electrical ROW operations
paras: Commitment to safety is the first key area of the 9 Arrow electrical right-of-way safety manual. The manual sets out 9 Arrow's dedication to maintaining the highest safety standards in electrical right-of-way operations, with safety policies aligned with OSHA standards.

sections.h2: Safety training for 9 Arrow ROW crews
paras: Training is the second key area of the 9 Arrow electrical right-of-way safety manual. The manual details training for employees in hazard recognition, electrical awareness, first aid, equipment operation and emergency procedures.
The 9 Arrow safety manual also describes daily tailgate meetings. Those meetings keep all crew members informed about job scopes, identified hazards and emergency procedures.

sections.h2: Ongoing evaluation and improvement of ROW safety
paras: Ongoing evaluation is the third key area of the 9 Arrow electrical right-of-way safety manual. The manual describes the processes in place for continuous evaluation of safety protocols, aimed at continuous improvement in safety measures and incident management.

sections.h2: How to get the electrical right-of-way safety manual
paras: 9 Arrow publishes the full electrical right-of-way safety manual as an eBook. Utility partners and contractors who want a copy can call (210) 247-8410 or email john@9arrow.com. The manual is part of 9 Arrow's [right-of-way clearing](right-of-way-clearing) and [utility land clearing](energy-utilities) work for utility companies, service providers and field contractors.

faqs.q: How can I get a copy of the 9 Arrow ROW safety manual?
faqs.a: You can get a copy of the 9 Arrow electrical right-of-way safety manual by calling (210) 247-8410 or emailing john@9arrow.com. 9 Arrow publishes the full manual as an eBook for utility partners, contractors and anyone who wants to prioritize safety in electrical right-of-way operations.

faqs.q: What happens in a 9 Arrow daily tailgate meeting?
faqs.a: A 9 Arrow daily tailgate meeting, as described in the electrical right-of-way safety manual, keeps all crew members informed about the job scope, the hazards identified for the work and emergency procedures. The manual presents those meetings as part of building a knowledgeable and prepared workforce.

faqs.q: What kind of right-of-way work does 9 Arrow do?
faqs.a: 9 Arrow clears rights-of-way for utility companies, service providers and field contractors, including gas pipelines, powerline corridors and waterlines. Corridors are typically 30 to 120 feet wide, often 90 feet or more, and routes can run for many miles. 9 Arrow also maintains rights-of-way with tractor and batwing equipment.
